meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why did Owen find out about a zero from the gradebook on his phone?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
People write in other programs and paste it in. I'm noting 11:52 and 11:58. Did anyone put this to Owen before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record, and it stays quiet. Is anything on his record right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
I'm reading the scene now. A student misquoting a line is a mistake, and it isn't proof of anything. Is that all this shows?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I've read the line and I'm not arguing about it. What are you proposing, and what is on his record today?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's what drafting is. You still haven't told me what's on his record, Hale.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, not because of anything he did. In writing tonight: private, nothing on his record, and the rewrite date in it before December 1.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth works. Put the time and who supervises in the email tonight, along with everything else.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on Owen's record. I still expect the time, the name of who supervises, and a straight answer on whether anything is on his record today. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, before December 1, replacing the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight with a time, a supervisor, and an answer on his record today; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and let her check it herself, which gave her something dated and specific instead of a score.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you ground, though you never answered her question about his record, which she asked three times.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your edit times of 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM on October 28 came close to that kind of late night, but that proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Answer her question about whether anything is on his record the first time she asks, so she has less reason to stay guarded.
